content:
Sara (Support): Heads-up — customer AcmeApp reported a sudden spike in hallucinations after our patch last night. They say prompts that previously returned terse factual answers are now verbose and creative. Escalating. https://tickets/acme/9876

Miguel (Eng): thanks. any sample request/response? did they pin sampling params in the call?

Sara (Support): pasted example from their app (redacted):

User: "List the steps to rotate a GCP service account key."
API request headers: Authorization: Bearer sk-live-abc123, model: open-llama-3-small, no temperature/top_p set in request.
API response (recent): long narrative with speculative steps and warnings about legal issues.
API response (before patch): short bullet list of exact commands.

Miguel (Eng): interesting — they did not set temperature or top_p explicitly so they relied on our server defaults.

deploy-bot: deploy completed: sampling-defaults-rollout v2 -> prod at 2026-05-18T03:12:08Z :white_check_mark:

Jules (SRE): was that rollout targeted? which customers were included?

Kevin (Infra): rollout was global for hosted API. We pushed a change to default sampling profile to align with new quality tests. The change was committed in config: 

```yaml
# before
default_sampling:
  temperature: 0.0
  top_p: 1.0
# after (rolled out)
default_sampling:
  temperature: 0.7
  top_p: 0.9
```

Miguel (Eng): whoa — that explains creative outputs. That should've been an opt-in. Why did we flip a global default?

Kevin (Infra): product-directed; aim was to reduce bland answers across models. Rollout notes said: "enable sampling defaults for generation quality". We missed targeted flag.

Alex (Product): I approved the experiment rollout but under the assumption it was limited to internal beta. My bad. We need immediate mitigation and a long-term rollback plan.

Miguel (Eng): mitigation plan: 1) provide customer with how-to to set request-level sampling to previous defaults (temp=0.0, top_p=1.0) in the short term; 2) hotfix to revert global default to previous values; 3) add a migration window + explicit opt-in moving forward.

Sara (Support): I started a reply draft to AcmeApp with repro steps and workaround. Will paste curl example for them to set explicit params on every call: 

```bash
curl -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate \
  -H 'Authorization: Bearer $API_KEY' \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -d '{"model":"open-llama-3-small","input":"List the steps to rotate a GCP service account key.","temperature":0.0,"top_p":1.0}'
```

Miguel (Eng): also capture server logs for that customer to measure the regression window. Sara, can you ask them for the request IDs or timestamps?

Sara (Support): asked them for request ids; they sent two: req_2234 and req_2261 (timestamps in window).

Jules (SRE): pulling logs for req_2234..2261 now. If global default was changed at deploy time we should see the header or effective sampling in the router logs.

Kevin (Infra): starting rollback to previous defaults on hosted control plane now. ETA ~15m. I'll post status.

deploy-bot: rollback action started: sampling-defaults-rollout v2 -> revert at 2026-05-18T03:50:12Z

Miguel (Eng): after rollback we should run A/B tests on a small cohort and notify customers clearly before toggling defaults. Also add a config flag "allow-global-defaults" off by default.

Alex (Product): agreed. I'll update the rollout playbook and add a mandatory "customer-impact-review" step for default changes.

Sara (Support): AcmeApp confirmed temporary workaround worked for one example after we guided them. They're waiting for official rollback and note they hit this in prod traffic. Requesting timeline and a postmortem.

Jules (SRE): logs show effective sampling header changed at 2026-05-18T03:12:08Z matching deploy-bot time. Responses between 03:12 and 03:50 contain increased token diversity and longer outputs.

Kevin (Infra): rollback complete at 2026-05-18T03:50:12Z. Monitoring metrics: average reply length and token entropy trending back to baseline.

Miguel (Eng): next steps (action items):
- Miguel: create hotfix PR to prevent global flips without a targeted cohort (owner: Miguel)
- Kevin: add safeguard in control plane that requires explicit "scope:" when changing defaults (owner: Kevin)
- Alex: coordinate customer comms and patch notes (owner: Alex)
- Sara: send customer postmortem and SLA remediation offer (owner: Sara)

Sara (Support): sending response now. Draft: "We reverted an accidental change to platform defaults that affected request-level behavior when temperature/top_p weren't set. We recognize the impact and will follow up with a full postmortem and remediation." Thoughts? :pray:

Alex (Product): good, add timeline and mention the workaround (explicit params) and that we rolled back. Keep tone apologetic but factual.

Miguel (Eng): also attach a short repro test they can run to confirm behavior: 

```python
# quick sanity check
from redwood import Client
c = Client(api_key='REDACTED')
print(c.generate('open-llama-3-small', 'List the steps to rotate a GCP service account key.', temperature=0.0, top_p=1.0))
```

Sara (Support): will send and request any additional failing examples. Will open a postmortem ticket and put it on the ops board.

Alex (Product): thanks everyone. Let's treat this as high priority for process change.

Miguel (Eng): filing PR now. I'll link it here when ready.

Sara (Support): tagging when customer replies. End of thread for now.
